samples: This program manages a small stock inventory in a SQLite file. It can open (and create if needed) the database, add a delivered amount to an existing item's stock, and query items whose quantity is at or below their reorder level, lowest first. As written, its entry point is not configurable: it always opens `data/inventory.db`, records a delivery of 500 units of the item with SKU "BOLT-10" (failing with an unknown-SKU error if that item doesn't exist), then prints either a "nothing to reorder" message or a line for each item still needing reorder. It therefore works as a library of reusable inventory functions, but the runnable program is more of a fixed demo than a general tool.

This program manages a small stock inventory in a SQLite file (`data/inventory.db`), creating the items table if it doesn't exist. When run, it adds a delivery of 500 units to the item with SKU "BOLT-10" (failing with an error if that SKU isn't in the table), then prints every item whose quantity is at or below its reorder level, lowest stock first, or a "nothing to reorder" message if there are none. It is really a fixed demo plus reusable functions for opening the database, finding low-stock items, and recording deliveries, so you would reuse those functions or change the hardcoded delivery rather than use it as a general-purpose tool.

This program manages a small stock inventory in a SQLite file. It can open the database (creating the items table if needed), add a delivered amount to an item's stock (failing with an unknown-item error if the item doesn't exist), and list items at or below their reorder level, lowest stock first. Its main routine is a fixed demonstration rather than a general tool: it opens a hard-coded database file, records one hard-coded delivery of 500 units to a specific item, and prints either "nothing to reorder" or the low-stock items. Be aware that it also reads and writes the filesystem, and that the delivery will fail unless that item already exists, since nothing in it adds new products.

This program manages a small stock inventory in a SQLite file, and its entry point adds a delivery of 500 units of one fixed product (BOLT-10) to `data/inventory.db`, creating the items table if it is missing. It then prints every item whose quantity is at or below its reorder level, lowest stock first, or says nothing needs reordering. Note that the delivery is hard-coded rather than taken from input, and it fails with an error if that product doesn't exist, so it works as a reusable set of database functions more than as a ready-to-use tool.

This program manages a small stock inventory in a SQLite file (data/inventory.db): it creates an items table if needed, and offers operations to add a delivered quantity to an item (failing with a clear error if the product doesn't exist) and to list items at or below their reorder level, lowest stock first. Its entry point is a fixed demo rather than a general tool: it records one hard-coded delivery of 500 units for one product, then prints either "nothing to reorder" or a line for each low-stock item. It's a useful starting point or library for inventory checks, but you would need to change the code to handle other products, amounts, or database locations, and as written it takes no input from the user.
